gaps.term: Tensor product of the single-bit butterflies (identity for building H_0 on all d bits)
gaps.quote: Applying $H_0$ to all $d$ selected bits is built by the [Tensor product](tensor-product.md) of the $d$ single-bit butterflies
gaps.note: The page asserts that applying the d single-bit butterflies one at a time, in any order, gives the same result as the tensor-product construction. It never states what the tensor product of these maps is or why it coincides with sequential application, so the reader cannot check the claim from the page.

gaps.term: Exactness of intermediate values as Gaussian dyadics
gaps.quote: Intermediate values in the layer are exact [Gaussian dyadic numbers](gaussian-dyadic.md)
gaps.note: The page does not say the inputs are dyadic, nor why halving (u+v)/2 and (u-v)/2 keeps values in that set or how many fractional bits p must allow for repeated halving. The claim is presented as fact without support.

gaps.term: Pointwise cost charged to the stored volume
gaps.quote: the source charges each such pass to the stored volume
gaps.note: This is a cost-accounting claim attributed to the source without a (cited) marker and without the accounting being stated, so the reader cannot check why each pass is O(V).

gaps.term: Summed cost bound O(d^lambda') and the swap exponents
gaps.quote: The sum is $O(d^{\lambda'})$ for any $\lambda'$ above the swap exponents and below 1.
gaps.note: The page does not define 'the swap exponents' (only a single exponent tau is given, for one swap), does not say how the groups of 'power-of-base sizes' are chosen or what base is meant, and does not show how summing the costs over O(log d) levels yields O(d^lambda') or why lambda' must lie above those exponents.
